composition.mass: The paper itself is the ground: cream tiles at three heights with charcoal dust settled in their pits, compressed charcoal sticks and grains lying on them like boulders, a rolled blending stump for a beacon.
composition.read: A walk across the paper tiles from the bitten southwest corner, stepping up two sheets past a fallen charcoal stick and the dust pits to the top sheet.

lighting.notes: raking lamp across a drawing board: Tooth only shows under light skimming the sheet, so the light is low and warm from one side and the background is the kraft board the sheet lies on.

rules: Leave the tiles open: no trees, only charcoal lumps and dust pits.
Keep the blending stumps beside the climb, never on the rim lip.
The top sheet around the bird stays clean paper.

shaper.name: patchwork
shaper.why: Cold-press tooth is a regular grid of raised paper and sunken pits; a patchwork of flat paper tiles at three heights, with holes bitten from the edge, is that grain enlarged until a visitor can walk on it.

surface_mix.why: Sand is the untouched paper (#dddddd reads warm on cold-press under lamp light), dirt is the dust settled into the tooth, stone the eraser-lifted paper, and a sliver of grass the sage of fixative spray.

cliff_treatment.why: A sheet seen edge-on: a cream paper band on top of the dark charcoal-stained board beneath it.

concept.name: aspect-tooth
concept.fragment: Round 5 reading authored by the build agent from pipeline/seed/analysis/forest.json and the drawing itself, without the analyzer (Gemini returns 402). One aspect of the charcoal drawing, "tooth", becomes the place; the shaper, palette, lighting, props and the figure's pose are argued from that aspect alone. It must not repeat the round-4 forest readings (ash basin with soot trunks, taproot knoll with charred boles, birch spiral) or their shapers (basin, mound, spiral).
